subject: science
cluster: The solar system and Earth's history
skillName: Orbital Motion in the Solar System
intro: Objects in the solar system, like planets and moons, move in orbits around a larger body because of gravity. A planet orbits the Sun, and a moon orbits a planet. Orbits are regular and repeating, so they can be predicted. Planets closer to the Sun orbit faster and take less time to go around (a shorter year), while planets farther out move slower and take much longer. Using patterns and simple math, we can predict where an orbiting object will be.

items.prompt: Why do planets orbit the Sun?

steps: An orbit is a curved path around a larger body.
The Sun's gravity pulls on the planets, keeping them in their paths.
So planets orbit the Sun because of the Sun's gravity.
solution.answer: Because the Sun's gravity pulls on them, keeping them in orbit around it.

items.prompt: A planet close to the Sun takes 1 year to orbit, and a far planet takes 80 years. What pattern does this show?

steps: Closer planets move faster and have shorter orbits.
The close planet orbits in 1 year while the far one takes 80 years.
So the pattern is that planets farther from the Sun take much longer to orbit.
solution.answer: Planets farther from the Sun take much longer to orbit than closer ones.

items.prompt: Because orbits are regular and repeating, what can we do with them?

steps: A repeating pattern can be used to predict the future.
Orbits repeat regularly, so we can calculate where an object will be later.
So we can predict the motion and position of orbiting objects.
solution.answer: We can predict where an orbiting object will be, because its motion repeats regularly.

items.prompt: What keeps a moon orbiting a planet?

steps: A moon circles a planet in an orbit.
The planet's gravity pulls on the moon, keeping it in orbit.

items.prompt: Earth takes 1 year to orbit the Sun. If a planet is twice as far and orbits much more slowly, is its year longer or shorter than Earth's?

steps: Planets farther from the Sun orbit more slowly and take longer.
This planet is farther and slower than Earth.
So its year (one orbit) is longer than Earth's.
solution.answer: Longer than Earth's year, because it is farther from the Sun and orbits more slowly.

items.prompt: Use the pattern of orbital motion to explain how we can predict a planet's position next year.

steps: Each planet takes a fixed, repeating time to orbit the Sun.
Knowing that time and the planet's current position, we can calculate how far it moves in a year.
So we can predict where the planet will be next year using its regular orbital motion.
solution.answer: Because each planet orbits in a fixed, repeating time, we can calculate from its current position where it will be next year.
